findings.text: Descriptor factories create EL2, timer and identification entries from a common shape. Each entry selects guest access logic, reset logic, backing storage, user read logic, user write logic, visibility logic and a base value. EL2 forms default to EL2 visibility, with separate forms for normal and VNCR and redirected traps, while timer forms bind timer access with timer user helpers.

Identification entries share default behaviour. Guest access uses access_id_reg, user reads use get_id_reg, user writes use set_id_reg, visibility uses id_visibility, and reset uses the sanitised reader. Concrete forms keep those defaults while varying only the base mask, with filtered forms substituting a custom setter and AArch32 forms substituting AArch32 visibility.

Hidden and unallocated identification slots are concealed from the guest. Hidden forms reuse the normal identification descriptor but force RAZ visibility with a zero base. Unallocated forms synthesize a name from the CRm and Op2 numbers, fix the encoding class to the identification space, reuse the default identification callbacks, and likewise force RAZ visibility with a zero base.

A register descriptor logically holds an encoding or name, a guest trap callback, a reset callback, a storage index, user read and write callbacks, a visibility predicate and a base value. A trap parameter block logically holds a direction flag plus a value word exchanged with the guest. The fragments show those slots populated for debug, control, translation, fault, performance and identification classes.

Traps for SP_EL1 and SPSR_EL1 and CNTKCTL_EL1 move a value word directly with the low level helpers, while ELR_EL1 moves through the vcpu read and write wrappers. Writes store the incoming word and reads return the stored word, and each handler reports success.

HCR reset starts from the descriptor base value and sets the E2H bit when the NV1 capability is absent on the CPUs, then stores the result into the slot selected by the descriptor and returns the stored value.

Visibility predicates hide features the VM lacks. A shared EL2 wrapper returns the EL2 gate result when visible and otherwise defers to a feature predicate. Specializations require EL2 visibility plus a feature such as SVE or SCTLR2 or S1POE or S1PIE or TCR2, or a nested virtualization fraction such as NV2 only or NV3, or fine grained trap levels, while CNTHV instead requires nested virtualization without E2H0 mode. When requirements fail the result is hidden.

ZCR_EL2 guest access first checks whether nested SVE traps are enabled for the vcpu. When enabled it injects a nested SVE trap and reports not handled. Otherwise reads return the stored EL2 slot and writes update that slot, reporting handled.

Guest accesses to VTR and MISR and EISR and ELRSR are read only. Writes are rejected through the read only helper. Reads return the sanitized guest VTR for VTR and the computed maintenance values for the other three.
Guest VTR is derived from the host interrupt controller VTR by clearing bits under the EL2 RES0 mask and setting bits under the EL2 RES1 mask.
EISR and ELRSR getters each compute a shared maintenance state block for the vcpu and then project one field from it, so both reflect the same snapshot computation.

MDCR_EL2 reads return the stored value. Writes decode the HPMN field, limit it to the VM counter count when out of range, write back the clamped value, and request a PMU reload when the HPME bit changed between old and new values. MDCR reset stores the VM counter count and returns it.

RAS fault record traps form a small gate. A v1p1 subset including format, control, flag and extended misc encodings requires either RAS v1p1 or RAS base plus the fractional RAS bit, otherwise an undefined exception is injected and the trap reports not handled. Remaining RAS encodings require RAS base support with the same undef behaviour. Admitted accesses behave as read as zero and write ignored.

Implementation identification registers MIDR and REVIDR and AIDR support a VM scoped writable mode. Guest writes are rejected. When the writable flag is set, guest reads delegate to the generic identification path; otherwise REVIDR and AIDR reads return host values while other encodings warn. Reset returns boot CPU values per encoding and signals a bug otherwise. User writes hold the configuration lock, succeed without change when the value already matches, otherwise require the writable flag, reject changes after the VM has run, reject bits outside the descriptor mask, and then store the VM wide value.
User writes to implementation identification registers serialize on the VM configuration lock held through a scoped guard for the whole compare and validate and store sequence.
SCTLR_EL1 table entry seeds reset with value 0x00C50078.
Implementation identification writable masks cover the low 32 bits for MIDR_EL1 and all 64 bits for REVIDR_EL1, while AArch32 identification writables cover the low 32 bits.

The system register table enumerates debug breakpoint and watchpoint groups, debug control, implementation and architectural identification registers across AArch32 and AArch64 spaces, control and translation and fault and performance and interrupt classes, each entry binding trap, reset, storage, user and visibility handlers appropriate to its class.
Out of range HPMN writes do not fault; the value is silently clamped to the supported counter count, matching the architectural unknown treatment while keeping emulation simple.
A trap for an EL2 register that arrives at the EL1 handler indicates a misconfigured trap and is reported through the bad trap path rather than emulated.
